front: What is the purpose of a stain in a temporary mount?
back: To increase contrast so that nearly transparent structures (nucleus, walls) become visible.

front: Stain for onion epidermis? Stain for cheek cells?
back: Iodine solution for onion (and starch); methylene blue for cheek cells.

front: Why lower a coverslip at an angle?
back: So the liquid pushes air out ahead of it and no air bubbles are trapped.

front: Structures found in plant cells but not animal cells?
back: Cellulose cell wall, plasmodesmata, chloroplasts (in photosynthetic cells), large permanent vacuole with tonoplast.

front: Structure found in animal cells but not flowering-plant cells?
Carbohydrate store in plant cells and in animal cells?
back: Starch grains in plants; glycogen granules in animals.

front: Why put used cheek-cell swabs into disinfectant?
back: Body fluids may carry pathogens; disinfectant kills them. Use only your own cells.

front: What do all cells use as their immediate energy source?
back: ATP made in respiration, for active transport, protein synthesis, movement and division.

front: Why can onion bulb cells not show chloroplasts?
back: They grow underground without light, so no chloroplasts develop; a stain is needed to see their structures.
